title: Emergency card replacement while traveling
summary: This document explains emergency replacement for a lost or stolen abroad debit card: after reporting, a replacement can typically reach you within 2 days (subject to courier availability/location). It also covers blocking the card, monitoring delivery updates, updating recurring payments, and obtaining a bank-issued cashier’s check for a $8 fee. It further lists debit card decline code guidance for physical/card-data issues (Code 82: chip/CVV mismatch; Code 87: declined due to cash back not permitted, with advice to retry without cash back and use Rho-Bank ATMs for free cash).
faqs: If my card is lost or stolen while traveling abroad, how fast can an emergency replacement arrive and what affects timing?
What steps should I take to request an emergency replacement, including what address and updates I need to provide?
If I need money before the replacement arrives, can you provide a cashier’s check and what is the fee?
After I report my card, will it be blocked, and do I need to update recurring payments?
What does debit decline code 82 mean (negative CAM/CVV results) and what should I do if my card seems damaged vs undamaged?
What does decline code 87 mean (purchase amount only, no cash back), and how can I complete a purchase or get cash?
